chapter: Lover Man and the postwar years
title: "Mad About You" and "I Refuse to Sing the Blues"
summary: Ann Cornell revived "Mad About You" in Philadelphia; Ramirez talks about his other song with Jimmy and Helen Humes's version.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, to make an observation, it's too bad that Jimmy had to go to Paris. I mean, if he had been around more, I think a lot of things would have happened with him and I as far as writing is concerned.
Now, nothing much happened with "Mad About You", did it?
It's a great song, you know.
Well, Ann Cornell(?) did it in Philadelphia. It took off... This was back in the Fifties, I think. Ann Cornell. I was in the picture with her...
Well, it was (?) Cafe Society outside. And she did "I Refuse To Sing The Blues," which is another song that I did with Jimmy(?).
Well, that's another one. You know the record Helen Humes made of that...
I'll make a cassette for you.
It's very nice. I have told her several times, 'That suits you, and nobody else has really done anything with it; you should work on that.' Because...
See, the title is a little misleading. "I Refuse To Sing The Blues," yeah, but the thing is, it's a little more intimate than that. You know, I don't want to complain all the time!
I know. But that's the point. But it still has a sort of Blues quality.
